transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Celestia), Marcus Green (ML Eng), Priya Shah (Infra Lead)

Summary: quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria and the integration approach. focus on function-calling/structured outputs and benchmark plan.

00:00 Lena: okay thanks everyone for joining, um we're excited to hear how Redwood might fit into our inference stack
00:10 Maya: thanks lena, yeah maybe quick intros and then we'll jump into what success looks like on your side and then talk integration and benchmarks
00:20 Marcus: i'm marcus, lead ml engineer, we'll be running the benchmark and integrating into our pipeline, priya handles infra
00:30 Priya: hey all, i'll be validating network and security requirements, we have strict VPC/KMS needs
00:40 Ravi: great. quick agenda: success criteria, traffic and token volumes, benchmark plan, then integration details — SDKs and openai-compatible endpoints + function calling and structured output formatting

02:05 Lena: on success criteria: we care about p95 latency for single-turn calls under 200ms for short prompts (~200 tokens), throughput at peak of ~350 concurrent requests, and extraction accuracy for structured outputs > 92% on our validation set. cost target is also important — want to understand unit economics for 1M tokens/month and also for burst scenarios
02:40 Maya: that aligns with what we've seen for other fintech customers. to confirm — p95 <200ms for short prompts, throughput 350 concurrent, extraction accuracy 92%+. any hard requirements on model size or we can propose variants?
02:55 Marcus: we want to test 7B and 13B model variants initially. accuracy vs latency tradeoff is key. also need function calling for some of the structured extraction (we run downstream actions if parse confidence > x)
03:20 Ravi: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints that accept function-calling style payloads; our SDKs (python/node) have helpers for registering function schemas and parsing structured outputs. small note — the auto transcript might show 'Redwood API' but sometimes docs call it Redwood Hosted or Dedicated endpoints depending on deployment
03:45 Priya: for pilot we prefer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private. our security team will ask for SOC 2 docs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, and audit logs retention policy. are those available?
04:00 Maya: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations; can share security pack. Dedicated gives the predictable throughput and VPC options, Private is possible for air-gapped environments but takes longer to set up

06:10 Marcus: workload sizing — current production traffic is around ~200 RPS average, peaks 400 RPS, average prompt 180 tokens, average response 120 tokens; projected pilot traffic will be synthetic 1000 requests over 1 hour to validate throughput. need to size GPU pool for 7B/13B models for those numbers
06:40 Ravi: for sizing we usually recommend the following: for 7B baseline, a single A100 equiv GPU can handle ~800-1.2k concurrent lightweight requests depending on batching and kv cache. for 13B you should expect roughly 40-60% lower throughput per-GPU. we'll include a sizing sheet with recommended Dedicated pool configs and estimated token/sec costs
07:05 Lena: benchmarks — we want an apples-to-apples comparison against OpenAI/Anthropic. can you provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so we can run our existing scripts?
07:20 Ravi: absolutely — we provide OpenAI-compatible REST routes and sample curl/python/node scripts. we'll also provide streaming examples and webhook fallbacks. the benchmark runbook will show how to run latency/throughput tests and structured output scoring; we'll include both JSON schema-based function-calling examples and raw text extraction examples

09:10 Priya: about function calling — does the Redwood endpoint strictly follow OpenAI function calling spec or are there differences? we have a bunch of infra tooling expecting that format
09:25 Ravi: our endpoints are compatible for the most part; we support registering functions and the runtime will return structured JSON plus a confidence/score field. small differences: we add a redwood_trace_id in responses and our streaming chunks include token-level timing metadata. i'll surface those in the docs. sometimes model-specific outputs need post-processing, but we'll include examples
09:50 Marcus: nice. for structured outputs we need determinism for certain fields — can we pin model variants and use deterministic sampling?
10:05 Maya: yes, you can pin model versions and set sampling/determinism parameters. for production you'll likely use temperature 0 and beam-like decoding where supported; we also recommend evals to detect regressions during rollouts

12:15 Lena: timeline — We're aiming to run a 2-week pilot followed by a 4-week benchmark before a Q4 procurement decision. can Redwood support that timeline?
12:30 Maya: yes — typical timeline: week 0 (setup + security review + VPC peering), week 1-2 pilot (functional + latency checks), week 3-6 extended benchmarks and quality evaluation, then decision. we'll prioritize getting Dedicated capacity reserved for pilot window to match your concurrency needs
12:55 Priya: how long for VPC peering and KMS config? our network team needs to plan firewall rules
13:10 Ravi: VPC peering + private networking usually 5-10 business days depending on approvals; KMS integrations are straightforward if you have a cloud KMS — we support AWS KMS and bring-your-own-key options. we'll send a checklist for firewall ports and subnets

15:00 Marcus: benchmarks — scoring extraction accuracy: we'll send 1k labeled examples, want you to run function-calling pipeline and return structured JSON; we'll compute precision/recall. also want token cost metrics and latency per model variant
15:25 Ravi: great, we'll run the function-calling pipeline in the benchmark and output both the raw model JSON and the parsed object; we'll add per-request token usage to the logs so you can compute unit economics

17:40 Lena: what about latency expectations for streaming vs non-streaming? some of our UI components rely on streaming partial results
17:55 Ravi: streaming tends to increase perceived latency for the user but reduces time-to-first-byte; for short responses we can often hit p95 <200ms non-streaming on Dedicated with small models; streaming is good for long outputs and interactive UIs. we'll include streaming examples in the runbook

20:10 Priya: compliance: we need audit logs and retention of request metadata for 1 year, and proof that data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys
20:25 Maya: we can provide audit log exports and support KMS-backed encryption. retention and export formats we'll cover in the security pack we send

23:00 Marcus: is there an easy path to integrate via existing openai clients in our codebase? refactor minimal effort
23:15 Ravi: yes, our OpenAI-compatible endpoints mean minimal changes — typically swapping the base URL and API key. our SDKs wrap the differences and include helper functions for function-calling and structured output parsing. we'll attach a migration guide with sample diffs for python/node

25:40 Lena: outstanding risks/objections? cost ballpark, accuracy vs latency vs cost tradeoff, and time to set up VPC/KMS
26:00 Maya: we'll surface unit economics for both Hosted + Dedicated and show sensitivity to batch size and quantization. for Private-on-prem we can discuss later if Dedicated doesn't meet data residency needs

29:10 Ravi: one more technical note — KV cache/prefix caching can dramatically reduce token usage for chat-like flows; if your workload is repetitive we can configure automatic prefix caching in the runtime to lower cost and improve latency
29:35 Marcus: that could help with our 50% repeated prompts case, nice

33:00 Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send pricing + sizing sheet, security docs, the benchmark runbook and sample scripts, and schedule a kickoff for 2026-09-01 if you confirm pilot window.
33:20 Lena: yes please, and we'll aim to provide prompt sets and labeled examples by 2026-08-24. we'll confirm network contacts for VPC peering

34:10 Priya: action items noted, i'll loop in our network team after we get your firewall checklist

35:00 Maya: any other Qs?
35:10 Marcus: one tiny thing — does Redwood support model quantization or lower-precision runtime for cost savings?
35:25 Ravi: yes, we have quantized runtime paths and can recommend quantization profiles per model. we'll include that in the sizing/cost sheet — note it can affect accuracy so we'll include quality checks in the benchmark

37:00 Lena: thanks all, this was helpful. look forward to the docs and runbook
37:10 Maya: thanks folks, we'll follow up with all materials by EOD tomorrow (2026-08-21) and Ravi will share the runbook earlier
37:25 Meeting end
